bands.label: Hike to 1.0%
bands.summary: BOJ raises the policy rate to 1.0%, the highest level since 1995, while the Fed and RBA hold steady the same week.

bands.label: Exit from negative rates
bands.summary: BOJ ends its negative interest rate policy and runs a slow series of hikes as inflation and wage growth persist.

bands.label: Abenomics and QQE
bands.summary: Kuroda-era quantitative and qualitative easing under Abenomics locks in sustained ultra-loose policy and a swollen BOJ balance sheet.

bands.label: Lost decades and ZIRP
bands.summary: After the 1995 cut to historic lows, Japan moves through zero interest rate policy and early quantitative easing across two decades of weak growth and deflation.

frames.label: Jun 2026 hike
frames.note: The story begins with the 17 June 2026 announcement that the Bank of Japan policy rate now sits at 1.0%. Read this way, the news is a fresh data point in current monetary policy and a contrast to the Fed and RBA holds the same week. Market wire desks and breaking-news headlines tend to open here.

frames.label: Mar 2024 exit
frames.note: The story begins in March 2024, when the Bank of Japan ended its negative interest rate policy. Read this way, the latest hike is one more scheduled step in a normalization cycle that has been running for over two years. Central-bank trackers and policy analysts often open here.

frames.label: 1995 baseline
frames.note: The story begins in 1995, when Japanese policy rates last sat near this level before the long descent. Read this way, the headline marks the close of a 31-year chapter of ultra-loose money rather than a routine meeting. Long-horizon macro historians and structural commentators tend to open here.
